text:
mike: Heads-up — prototyping a 'plug-and-play' routing shim for service keys. Idea: let users attach a small 'routing intent' to a key (latency-priority, cost-saver, region-pref) and the platform routes to the best pool. Want console + telemetry UX input before we flip flags.
anya: Curious — is this metadata on the key or an extra API param?
mike: Metadata on the service key. No API param changes for callers; routing is resolved server-side at auth time.
rupert: Main worry: silent routing changes that affect billing or SLOs. Console needs clear audit + per-key metrics (cost, latency) and a rollback path.
sasha: Agree. Also opt-in by default for orgs — no surprise cost spikes.
jordan: Could we expose the resolved route in a response header like `X-Redwood-Route: pool-nyc-v2`? Helps debug.
mike: Good call. We'll add a header. Need to ensure it contains no PII and is short.
pm-elaine: UX idea: in key details show a 'Routing intent' dropdown, recent routing history sparklines, and a small explainer about tradeoffs (cost vs latency).
anya: Also show aggregated 'decision reasons' (capacity, regional preference, quota) with percentages.
mike: Telemetry plan: per-key metrics: `route.count`, `route.latency.p95`, `route.tokens.cost`. We'll also sample ~1% of full requests (payloads) to validate quality regressions when routing to cheaper variants.
rupert: 1% seems ok to start, but we need an opt-out for regulated tenants. Must be configurable org-level.
sasha: Rollout plan suggestion: feature flag at org-level. Canary 5 orgs → 20 → wider, gated on error rate & cost deltas.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for flags: routing-shim=true for orgs [redwood-labs, test-corp]. :rocket:
jordan: Alerting: create console alerts when `route.latency.p95` exceeds baseline by 30% and when eval-based quality regressions occur. Also surface cost delta per-key weekly.
mike: One open question: how much of route surface do we expose in docs? We should avoid apps depending on route names.
anya: Strongly agree — doc note: route identifiers are internal/opaque and may change.
pm-elaine: UX copy suggestion: 'Routing intent is advisory. Enabling may cause traffic to use different model variants — monitor cost and quality before enabling.'
mike: I'll draft the copy.
rupert: Engineering tasks: add `routing.intent` tag to traces, attach `fallback.reason` enum to logs when we deviate, and ensure quota attribution stays with original key/org.
mike: Confirmed: quota attribution remains unchanged — only routing is different.
sasha: Edge case: service-account keys used by infra automation. Defaulting them to latency-priority might blow spend. Maybe `balanced` default and org override.
mike: Default will be `balanced`. Org-level override + per-key explicit setting.
anya: Also record `fallback.reason` (capacity, model-incompatible, region-unavailable) in telemetry so we can analyze patterns.
mike: Agreed — enumerated reasons persisted.
deploy-bot: Canary complete — 2 orgs healthy, no regressions observed. :white_check_mark:
pm-elaine: Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00 to review initial dashboards and copy?
mike: Done, invite sent to eng-platform + product.
rupert: Thanks — we'll need a lightweight dashboard tile per-org that shows routing mix and cost impact.
mike: Will add tile to the 'Keys' console view and to the per-org dashboard.
